title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight
label: Classy Joey Boy
how: Lost to Randall Crane in a Stretcher match at Birthday Bash.
note: Won at Ghosts of RAW on 31 October 2002, the Vegas Unification Match against The Maquilladora that merged the BlackJack and T3 titles into this championship.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight
label: "The Revolution" Randall Crane
how: Won a Stretcher match when Classy Joey Boy missed a spear off the top of the ambulance and rolled into it himself.
note: Retained by disqualification against Demonic on Firestorm 09-24-03; retained again by pinfall (a small package reversing the Sugar Blaster) against Classy Joey Boy at Vegas Violence III; survived a steel cage escape match between the two men's own allies, Thunder Valenkov and Demonic, on Firestorm 10-21-03; then lost the title to Classy Joey Boy in a No Disqualification, fall-count-anywhere match on Firestorm 10-28-03 after Daniel Sinz struck the champion's own surgically fragile knee with a sledgehammer early in that same match -- payback, by the broadcast's own account, for Crane's interference in Sinz's Birthday Bash stretcher match. The loss returned Crane to an in-storyline suspension both men had been serving since Vegas Violence III's own post-match assault.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Sebastian
how: Won the one-night tournament's four-way final, pinning Zell Strife after Tai Angela spat fire in Strife's face; the first 24 Hour Champion.
note: Lost while wrestling masked, pinned by Kerry Powell on 22 August 2001.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: "24 Karat" Kerry Powell
how: Pinned the masked man, unmasked afterward as the champion Sebastian; President Rob Beauty declared Powell champion.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Demonic and Blaze
how: Won the Tag Team Title Tournament final over Triple X.
note: Retained by count-out against Jack Spade and Dage on 24 October 2001. In Rage In The Cage Dage pinned Blaze and took his half of the titles.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Demonic and Dage
how: Dage took Blaze's half of the titles by pinning him in Rage In The Cage.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Triple X
how: Won a three-way title match, pinning Demonic with the Double Double after Dage left his partner alone.
note: No later 2001 document records the reign's end.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Blaze and Real Deal
how: Blaze pinned Chumpy with the Uncontrollable Inferno in a four-way brawl, a title change from Triple X.
note: Retained on 24 January by disqualification and at Ghost Town Blues in a Tornado Rules match against Triple X.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick

won.source: wave-C03-STRUCTURE-45's own titles-corrections-vwf-vegas-2003.json establishes that Kilpatrick won the title's own five-man qualifying tournament final at Vegas Violence III (dated to the month, no exact card date stated in the document itself) by submission over Johnny Freil; no reigns row was filed for that wave's own finding, left open until this pass's own Day Five title match required it.

how: Lost the VWF Submission Championship to Daniel Sinz by submission (Millennium Deathlock) in a title match during Group A of the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Five, after Sinz opened the match with an unsanctioned chair shot before the bell and battered the bleeding champion for its duration.
note: Also billed across the tournament's own broadcasts as holding a self-proclaimed, non-sanctioned "Sinz Days" belt alongside the Submission Championship; that belt is not modeled as a museum title record.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Sebastian
how: Pinned Kerry Powell in a roster-wide brawl, under the title's defend-anywhere rule.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight
label: Classy Joey Boy
how: Won by submission (Sugar Blaster) in a No Disqualification, fall-count-anywhere match after Randall Crane's own surgically fragile knee buckled attempting a Revolution's End powerbomb, worsened when Daniel Sinz struck the knee with a sledgehammer early in the same match.
note: His third VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship reign; the loss returned Randall Crane to an in-storyline suspension both men had been serving since Vegas Violence III's own post-match assault. The Maquilladora's own scheduled challenge on the Kickoff Card (9 January 2004) was called off by order of new co-owner Classy Joey Boy, who ruled he had already beaten The Maquilladora and would not face him again; Demonic and The Maquilladora wrestled a 24 Hour Contender Match instead, which The Maquilladora won. An unseen figure attacked the champion near a creek before Ghost Town Blues's own Pentagon match, keeping him from a scheduled title defense against the match's own winner; a stand-in triple threat settled that night's own live crowd stakes without changing the title. On Firestorm (26 Feb 2004), 50% owner Rob Beauty ruled the champion out at least six weeks with a concussion and declared the title vacant pending a Gauntlet tournament; Lark Fenriz later confessed on the same broadcast to being the attacker.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Daniel Sinz
how: Won the VWF Submission Championship from Yancy Kilpatrick in a title match during Group A of the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Five.
note: Retained by submission (Pinnacle of Excellence) against Marcel Klutz on the Kickoff Card (9 January 2004), after taunting the crowd's chants for the late Yancy Kilpatrick; after the bell, Kilpatrick's own entrance music played over the arena sound system and the crowd again chanted for him, unsettling Sinz. A challenge from "Maniac" Mike Wolfe at Ghost Town Blues (19 Feb 2004) ended without a decision when the presumed-dead Kilpatrick reappeared alive and struck Sinz with Wolfe's own prosthetic leg, Sinz fleeing before a finish; the champion retains by default.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Maquilladora

lost.note: Not lost in a match: VWF President Rob Beauty stripped Maq of the title off-page, ruling that a single man cannot hold a Tag Team Championship, after pressure from Randall Crane; the promotion's own Update for 24 May reports the stripping as already accomplished, so the exact date is not established beyond sometime between 16 and 23 May.

how: pinfall (Permanent Daylight), a handicap match against Blaze and the Real Deal (ended: stripped-vacated)
note: Defended alone as the VWF's own "one man tag team champion" against 28th Street, Sonicman and CAPSMAN, and Tai Angela and Blackbird.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: "The Ace" Jack Spade
how: Pinned Sebastian at Vegas Violence.
note: Retained against Corey Fuller and Dage on 17 October 2001.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Sex Icons
how: pinfall, Sebastian schoolboyed Father Frank O'Shea last in a fatal four-way for the vacant titles
note: The promotion's own last show before becoming RAW-Vegas.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Fallen Angels
how: Won the third fall of a three-title match against The Sex Icons and The Maquilladora.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Classy Joey Boy & Maul
how: Won from The Fallen Angels when Sebastian placed Classy Joey Boy on Xtreme Tony Cage for the count.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Zell Strife
how: Pinned Jack Spade with a leap from the top of the two-story cage in Rage In The Cage at Phear Phantastic.
note: Retained against Jack Spade and Corey Fuller on 15 November 2001.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Demonic
how: Pinned Zell Strife after Thomas Rainka's swing with the belt hit Strife by mistake.
note: No later 2001 document records the reign's end.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Dage
how: Pinned Demonic with the Revolution after Jack Spade and G-Gangsta's ringside brawl distracted him.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: The Maquilladora
how: Made Iyasu Saku submit to the Bow and Arrow during the Gauntlet battle royal, winning the VWF Submission Championship as a side stipulation of that match.
note: Won a Loser Retires, I Quit match over Demonic earlier the same broadcast, ending Demonic's own career, before winning the Submission Championship in the closing battle royal. Retained the title by disqualification against Daniel Sinz on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after Sinz struck her with a chair. Lost the title to Sonicman on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) in a triple threat also involving Sebastian, Sonicman applying the Camel Clutch after a run-in by The Equalizer chair-shotted Sebastian out of the match.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Sonicman
how: Applied the Camel Clutch to champion The Maquilladora for the submission in a triple threat also involving tag partner Sebastian, whom Sonicman turned on after a run-in by The Equalizer chair-shotted Sebastian out of the match.
note: Won the title on the same broadcast where his own tag partner Sebastian was chair-shotted out of the match by a run-in from The Equalizer. Lost it back to The Maquilladora off-page sometime before Wrestle Style V.2.

lost.source: The Maquilladora is already billed VWF Submission Champion again by Wrestle Style V.2 (27 August 2004); no document in the held record shows the change directly, matching this title's own established pattern of off-page changes.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Xtreme Tony Cage & Randall Crane

lost.source: Billed as champions at Ghosts of RAW (31 October 2002); no later change is recorded in 2002.

how: Won from Classy Joey Boy and Maul with Crane's Revolutions End 2000 powerbomb.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight
label: The Equalizer
how: Pinned champion Lark Fenriz, freshly chair-shotted by guest referee Flash, after stablemate Orion pulled him clear of a Jason Storm cover attempt earlier in the three-way and restored the match's own original referee.
note: Retains against The Maquilladora and Classy Joey Boy in a triple threat on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), pinning Classy Joey Boy with the Face Plant after Sebastian's own interference and a guest-referee stint from majority owner Kingston Cash. Retains again over Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora in a Wheel Of Chaos match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) after a doctor secretly working for Kingston Cash injects both challengers mid-match; the doctor is revealed afterward as Kingston Cash's own brother, Terrance Cash. A scheduled defense against Kagedo at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) never begins: Gods Tears attacks Kagedo with a tire iron during his own entrance, and John Tyler books a bonus tag match in its place, in which The Equalizer and Gods Tears are disqualified against Kagedo and Roadkill Rick. Retains again at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), entering the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal first by his own request rather than last as tradition dictates, and surviving as the sole man left in the ring after Thunder Valenkov, sent into a top rope that Hot Property forgets to pull down, goes over instead.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Rhombus

won.source: Attested as champions from the wing's own earliest surviving broadcast (Dog Day Five, 11 July 2003) onward; no document in the held record states when or how they won it.

how: Lost the titles between Birthday Bash (retained there in a TLC triple threat, 1 August 2003) and Firestorm 09-12-03, where Classy Joey Boy is already billed as tag champion; the title change itself is not present anywhere in the held record.
note: A genuine gap in the surviving record, not an omission of this pass's own reading.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Gods Tears
how: Submitted champion The Maquilladora with the Drunken Rage in a fall of the Rage in the Cage.
note: Won under the billed name Gods Tears, the same performer previously billed Orion The Hunter. Loses the title in a three-way at Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) also involving Sidious The Clown and Lark Fenriz, after the referee mistakes Fenriz's own hand slapping a concourse counter for the champion's tap-out; the VWF Hardcore Championship, also on the line, goes unaddressed in the decision.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Sidious The Clown
how: Awarded the VWF Submission Championship after the referee, guided through the finish by a bleeding Lark Fenriz, mistook Fenriz's own hand slapping a concourse counter for champion Gods Tears's tap-out during a three-way brawl that spilled from the ring through the backstage area.
note: The VWF Hardcore Championship, also on the line in the same match, goes unaddressed in the decision and stays with Gods Tears. Defended together with the VWF Hardcore Championship against Gods Tears and Lark Fenriz in a Scaffold Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005); wins the overall match by outlasting both other men on the scaffold, but the broadcast states neither title changes hands. Retains against Tazmanian Devil Mark McQueen at March To Madness (2 March 2005), putting McQueen out with a sleeper after an unexplained arena blackout leaves both men down. Defended against Fast Eddie Cutlass at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), declared a no contest after Gods Tears, Roadkill Rick, Adam Jennings and The Dark Monster Tai Angela all converge on Gods Tears mid-match. Loses the title to Roadkill Rick's own Texas Speedbump in an eight-man elimination match at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005) after Gods Tears attacks him from behind before the bell.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: "The Revolution" Randall Crane and Classy Joey Boy

won.source: A video-recap package on Vegas Violence III narrates the exact date and manner of this title change ("AUGUST 29, 2003 -- CJB uses a sledgehammer to help he and Crane win the Tag Team Titles from The Rhombus, Crane doesn't see it"); no primary broadcast dated 29 August 2003 is held in the held record, so the underlying match itself remains an in-fiction recap, not a served document, and no event id is cited.

how: Lost to The Rhombus on Firestorm 09-24-03 when Classy Joey Boy turned on his own partner, sledgehammering both CAPSMAN and Crane and placing Sonicman on top of Crane for the cover.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Demonic
how: Won the Pitz of Hell match in the Rhyolite silver mine, hitting the Pitz of Hell finisher after both men fell into an underground river.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight
label: Lark Fenriz

won.source: Billed as the reigning VWF Vegas Heavyweight Champion on Firestorm (3 May 2004) and throughout The Gauntlet 2004 (17 May 2004), where he retained in a Japanese Death Match; the title had been vacated on 26 February 2004 and no document in the held record shows how he won it.

how: Champion by the promotion's own billing after the February 2004 vacancy; the winning match is not in the held record.
note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing, on the same footing as the wing's other off-air title changes; the crowning show is absent from the record. Continues to be billed champion on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), scratched from his own three-way match by majority owner Kingston Cash before the bell; returns to competition, without the title on the line, in an eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Retains the title in a clean pin over Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004). The Heavyweight Championship main event on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) ends without a finish when a returning Classy Joey Boy interferes; Kingston Cash announces a random-draw title tournament running each week until Vegas Violence, with the champion defending every time he is drawn and the title changing hands on count-outs and disqualifications during it. Retains cleanly over a returning Billy Bones, a shell of his former self after months in an alcoholic rehabilitation facility, in the tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004). Wrestles The Predator Kevin Simmons to a time-limit draw in the tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004); majority owner Kingston Cash rules the count-out and disqualification stipulation does not cover draws, and both men advance. Retains in a fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) over Classy Joey Boy, Sebastian and The Assassin Marcus O'Malley (self-eliminated to save a kidnapped Mark McQueen), pinning Sebastian with the Sammael after Sebastian tricks Classy Joey Boy into a sledgehammer disqualification; the win sets a Vegas Violence main event against tournament runner-up The Equalizer. Signs the contract for that match on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), where a video appearance by Jason Storm inserts him into the match as a third man and the champion declares he no longer cares about the title, only about denying The Equalizer. Loses the title to The Equalizer in a three-way also involving Jason Storm at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), pinned after a chair shot from guest referee Flash; Orion's own interference in the match, and a referee dispute between guest referees Classy Joey Boy and Flash, both factor into the finish.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Rhombus
how: Won when Classy Joey Boy turned on tag partner and champion Randall Crane, sledgehammering him and placing Sonicman on top for the cover.
note: Lost the titles to the Rodeo Boys at Vegas Violence III after the returning Tai Angela's own interference (an arena blackout) let Kenny Kidd pin CAPSMAN.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Rodeo Boys
how: Won by pinfall after Tai Angela's own interference (the arena lights cut out) let Kenny Kidd pin CAPSMAN.
note: Retained by disqualification against The Legends of the VWF on Firestorm 10-21-03 and by pinfall against Superbeach and Dangerous J on Firestorm 10-28-03.

lost.source: No document read, or noted in any prior wave's own findings.md, narrates how or when the Rodeo Boys lost the titles.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Roadkill Rick
how: Submits champion Sidious The Clown with the Texas Speedbump in an eight-man elimination match also deciding the VWF 24 Hour and Hardcore Championships.
note: Wins the title as the first fall of the eight-man elimination match, then survives to see Hardcore Champion Gods Tears disqualified against him in a chair-and-brass-knuckles standoff.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: El Gringo Loco and Billy Bones
how: Won a four-way VWF Tag Team Championship Ladder match against outgoing co-champion Jushin Liger GOLD, the Legends of the VWF and the Fallen Angels; El Gringo Loco retrieved his own title belt, then shoved the ladder out from under Kenny Kidd so that his tag partner Billy Bones could claim the other belt.
note: The debuting Lynch Mob interfered against the Legends of the VWF mid-match, powerbombing Sebastian off a ladder and sending Sebastian and G-Gangsta's own ladder into the ropes. Retained without a decision on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004) against Hot Property (Hotstuff Stevie Knight and All That Austin Lee) after the referee called for the bell when an unidentified man entered the ring alongside a returning Kenny Kidd.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-hardcore
label: Gods Tears

won.source: Already billed the new VWF Hardcore Champion entering New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005); no document in the held record shows the off-page GT's Invitational he proposed to Kingston Cash on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), matching this wing's own established pattern of off-page title changes.

how: Already champion entering New Years Kick Off, defends no title match that night but is shown assaulting backstage vendor Spaz and special guest referee Sidious The Clown on the arena's own big screens with a lead pipe until new VWF guardian John Tyler orders him to stop under threat of a double title strip and suspension.
note: Not billed as contested in the VWF Hardcore and Submission Championship match on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), where the champion instead loses the VWF Submission Championship. Defended together with the VWF Submission Championship against Sidious The Clown and Lark Fenriz in a Scaffold Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005); Fenriz hits the ground first and the overall match goes to Sidious, but the broadcast states neither title changes hands, confirming Gods Tears retains the VWF Hardcore Championship. Retains against Roadkill Rick at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), a draw when neither man answers a ten count after a Cobra Clutch Suplex through a table. Retains again against Fast Eddie Cutlass at End Of March (30 March 2005), a time-limit draw. Retained without a change at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005): on the line, alongside the 24 Hour and Submission Championships, in the same eight-man elimination match, champion Gods Tears is disqualified against Roadkill Rick in a chair-and-brass-knuckles standoff, a finish that does not transfer the title.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: Iyasu Saku

won.source: The Gauntlet 2004 (17 May 2004) is the first document read by this wing's own accession lanes to bill Iyasu Saku, rather than Daniel Sinz, as the reigning VWF Submission Champion; no document in the held record shows the title actually changing hands.

how: Already champion entering the Gauntlet.
note: Retained against Kevin Simmons in a Hair vs. Hair match earlier the same broadcast, winning Simmons's own hair rather than defending it for a title change, then lost the championship by submission (Bow and Arrow) to The Maquilladora during the Gauntlet battle royal.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Rodeo Boys
how: Won the VWF Four Corners Tag Team Championship elimination match, Kenny Kidd pinning Stevie Knight after Billy Bones tripped him, once the champion Lynch Mob (eliminated first, LOCO submitting to Stevie Knight's sharpshooter) and The Unholy Alliance (eliminated second, Dementia pinned by Kidd) were both out.
note: Billy Bones wrestled the title match only two weeks after a ladder-match injury commentary had called career-threatening. Lost the title ten days later on Firestorm (27 May 2004), ambushed by Hot Property during a Flashback interview segment rather than in a sanctioned defense.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-submission
label: The Maquilladora

won.source: Already billed VWF Submission Champion entering Wrestle Style V.2 (27 August 2004); no document in the held record shows how she regained the title from Sonicman, matching this title's own established pattern of off-page changes.

how: Already champion entering Wrestle Style V.2, retained against Sebastian after Sonicman blindsided him with a foreign object before the referee could count.
note: No VWF Submission Championship match is held on Wrestle Style V.3. None is held on Wrestle Style V.4 or V.5 either, though she wrestles Fast Eddie Cutlass to a non-title time-limit draw on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) and loses to him in a seven-man mini rumble on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after an unidentified woman's own interference; Kingston Cash books Cutlass's own win in that rumble as a VWF Submission Championship match at Vegas Violence. Wrestles Fast Eddie Cutlass to a no contest at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), the scheduled title match halted after Orion, Orion #2 and The Equalizer run in and beat down both competitors. Retains despite a count-out loss to Gods Tears on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), the promotion's own house rule against count-out title changes keeping the belt with her.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: G-Gangsta
how: a fast count by VWF President Rob Beauty after a schoolboy on Demonic
note: Also holding the RCW Championship at the time, making him the only man to hold every VWF singles title.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Zell Strife
how: a three-way pinning G-Gangsta after both men traded chairshots and collapsed together
note: Retained the following night in a climb-the-cage match against Erik Andrews, and again 11 April against Andrews.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: G-Gangsta
how: a fast count by Rob Beauty after Gangsta schoolboyed Strife
note: Retained by disqualification 20 May against Erik Andrews and in a Rage In The Cage match 5 June against Sebastian.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Revolution Randall Crane
how: pinfall, after Sebastian chairshot G-Gangsta from ringside as he went up for the Gangsta Smash
note: The Sex Icons, Classy Joey Boy and Sebastian, physically took the belt from Crane afterward and presented it to Sebastian, though the referee's own decision named Crane champion.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Sebastian
how: Won the vacant title in the 24 Hour Title Tournament final, a series of falls against Van Wild and The Maquilladora; his third 24 Hour Title.
note: Lost the next night in the Ohio Valley promotion to Chris Hart, as shown at Phear Phantastic II.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Chris Hart
how: Won from Sebastian in the Ohio Valley promotion; billed at Ghosts of RAW as Ohio Valley and Vegas 24 Hour Champion.
note: The winning match itself is not held; Phear Phantastic II shows the footage.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat
label: G-Gangsta
how: Won the first Triple Threat Title match, pinning Bobby Silas after Jack Spade was counted out.
note: Retained at Vegas Violence (7 September 2001) and on 19 September 2001.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat
label: Zell Strife
how: Pinned Sebastian and then G-Gangsta in a three-way defense.
note: Retained on 24 October 2001 and through Rage In The Cage; on 15 November 2001 he handed the belt to Thomas Rainka, and Rob Beauty ruled him counted out.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat
label: Thomas Rainka
how: Pinned the Ghost in a barbed-wire three-way, after Zell Strife handed him the belt.
note: Retained on 22 November 2001, when he and the Real Deal were both counted out, and on 20 December 2001.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-bwf
label: Corey Fuller
how: Declared the winner by submission over Sebastian by Ric Beauty, refereeing; the first BWF Champion.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-bwf
label: G-Gangsta

lost.source: No 2001 document records the end of the reign.

how: Pinned Corey Fuller in a three-way.
note: Retained in Rage In The Cage (31 October 2001) and against the Legend of Xtreme (15 November 2001). By 20 December 2001 Classy Joey Boy holds the title; how it changed hands is not recorded.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-bwf
label: Classy Joey Boy

won.source: Champion by the 20 December 2001 Thursday Thunder; no document records when or how he won it.

lost.note: Not lost in a match: Ric Beauty sold his stake in the BWF back to Rob Beauty on air, and the belt was renamed the Blackjack Championship, with Classy Joey Boy continuing as champion under the new name.

note: Champion on 20 December 2001, retaining against Dage by double count-out; how he won it is not recorded.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Hot Property
how: Ambushed the champions during a Flashback interview segment, smashing Kenny Kidd through the set and finishing him with the Property Boom; host Flash then declared Hot Property the new champions.
note: Won the title outside a sanctioned bout, matching this title's own established pattern of off-page and recap-driven changes of hands. Lost it off-page sometime before Wrestle Style V.2 (27 August 2004), where Blaze and Real Deal are already billed champions; no document in the held record shows the change directly.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Alcoholics Anonymous
how: Mark McQueen submitted Real Deal with the Devils Snare after O'Malley and McQueen isolated an injured shoulder.
note: Lawyer RAR argues on behalf of the Rodeo Boys that the champions were never legitimate, since Billy Bones and Kenny Kidd were released rather than beaten for the belts; majority owner Kingston Cash reinstates the Rodeo Boys on the spot, who beat down the new champions with cowbells immediately after. No formal title reversal is shown. Retains against the Rodeo Boys on March To Hell (21 October 2004) when Kenny Kidd is disqualified for branding Marcus O'Malley with an iron; retains again on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) when a substitute Outlaw Morris Bass stands in for the hospitalized O'Malley and submits Billy Bones with the Devils Snare.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Mark McQueen and Kevin Simmons
how: Kevin Simmons pinned co-champion Marcus O'Malley in a fall of the Rage in the Cage; surviving co-champion Mark McQueen, who had already submitted Robbie Caldwell to defend his own half of the titles earlier in the same match, keeps his half and gains Simmons as his new partner.
note: No stable name is billed for the new pairing; Simmons and O'Malley are both members of the Society of Doom, which McQueen also runs with. Simmons's own half is later declared vacant after his suspension from the VWF, reported on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005) without an exact date.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-blackjack
label: Classy Joey Boy
how: Continued as champion when the BWF Championship was renamed the Blackjack Championship on air; a rename, not a title change in a match.
note: Retained against The Legend of Xtreme in a hardcore match on 17 January and against Tai Angela in a No Holds Barred match at Ghost Town Blues.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Jason Storm

lost.source: Still champion at Thunder of 14 November 2002, the latest 2002 card.

how: Won an elimination match against Chris Hart and James Kira with the Perfect Storm, taking the Ohio Valley title too.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Scott Starring

won.source: Attested as champion from the wing's own earliest surviving broadcast (Dog Day Five, 11 July 2003) onward; no document in the held record states when or how he won it.

how: Lost to Daniel Sinz on Firestorm 09-12-03.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Daniel Sinz
how: Won by pinfall with a rope-assisted sunset flip.
note: Successfully defended two-out-of-three-falls against Scott Starring at Vegas Violence III and in a fatal four-way against Cyn Bailus, El Gringo Loco and Jushin Liger GOLD on Firestorm 10-21-03, before losing the title to Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick in a 24 Hour/Submission title-for-title match on Firestorm 10-28-03 -- the referee counting Sinz's own arm down three times after Randall Crane knocked him unconscious with a sledgehammer, in retaliation for Sinz's own interference in Crane's Birthday Bash stretcher match.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov
how: Thunder Valenkov, a mystery entrant making a surprise return to the VWF, won a battle royal for the vacant half of the VWF Tag Team Championship left by suspended co-champion Kevin Simmons, eliminating Sebastian last to join titleholder Mark McQueen, who did not compete.
note: No stable name is billed for the new pairing. Retains over the Rodeo Boys in a Rings Of Glory match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), Thunder Valenkov pinning Kenny Kidd with the Thunder Bomb after Mark McQueen taps out to the Elko Lasso in his own half of the match. Loses the titles in an impromptu three-way tag match at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) when the debuting Team Brittania's own Simon Davidson pins Frank O'Shea, the challengers' own tag partner, rather than either champion; wins a rematch by disqualification against Team Brittania at End Of March (30 March 2005) after the returning Hot Property run in, but the disqualification does not itself return the titles.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Team Brittania
how: Debuting Team Brittania inserted themselves into a defense already underway between champions Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov and challengers Frank O'Shea and Billy Bones, turning it into a three-way; Justin Davidson pulled Valenkov from the ring to stop a cover on O'Shea, and Simon Davidson pinned O'Shea for the titles without either champion having been pinned.
note: Retains by disqualification against Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov at End Of March (30 March 2005) after the returning Hot Property (Stevie Knight and Austin Lee) run in and help finish McQueen. A legal challenge filed the same night argues the win itself does not count, since Team Brittania was never a named, signed participant in the St Patricks Day match; incoming VWF ownership is left to decide the championship's own status. On The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), Team Brittania defends the titles, billed with a question mark over their own legitimacy, against a returning Henry Fish (billed Scott Starring) and an unidentified stand-in wrestling as the absent Van Wild, winning by pinfall; the team's own hired ring announcer, not the broadcast's regular ring announcer, declares them champions afterward. The same night the previous champions, Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov, billed "the unlikely tag team champions," lose their own tag match to Hot Property when Valenkov turns on McQueen; the VWF's incoming ownership still has not ruled on the championship's own disputed status.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: El Gringo Loco and Jushin Liger GOLD

won.source: Already billed as reigning VWF Tag Team Champions by the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Twelve broadcast (18 December 2003) and again on the Kickoff Card (9 January 2004); no document read, or noted in any prior wave's own findings.md, establishes when or how they won the titles from the Rodeo Boys.

how: Already champions entering the Kickoff Card, retained against the debuting Fallen Angels (Tony Cage and Insomniac), El Gringo Loco pinning Tony Cage with a handful of tights.
note: The post-match chaos following this defense led directly into the Legends of the VWF/Rodeo Boys match and the debuting Lynch Mob's own attack on the Legends. Jushin Liger GOLD's own half of the championship changed hands in a four-way ladder match on Firestorm (19 January 2004), when Billy Bones climbed for the second belt while his own tag partner Kenny Kidd deferred; El Gringo Loco retained his own half by grabbing it for himself, recognized afterward as co-champion alongside Bones.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Rodeo Boys

won.source: A recap package on Firestorm (3 May 2004) names the Rodeo Boys (Billy Bones, re-paired with Kenny Kidd) as the reigning champions the Lynch Mob defeated to win the titles; no document in the held record shows the Rodeo Boys winning or defending the championship directly.

how: Already champions entering an untelevised Lynch Mob Lottery card not present in the held record.
note: Billy Bones's own re-pairing with his original Rodeo Boys partner Kenny Kidd, in place of outgoing co-champion El Gringo Loco, is itself undocumented; see vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team-r006's own note.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat

how: Pinned Thomas Rainka with the Bottom Line after Zell Strife knocked Rainka out with brass knuckles.
note: Retained on 17 January by double count-out against Zell Strife and Thomas Rainka in an impromptu title defense, and again on 24 January by double count-out against Xtreme Tony Cage.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat
label: Xtreme Tony Cage
how: Pinned Zell Strife after Thomas Rainka set both men on fire with a lit chair, in a three-way T3 Title match also involving Erik Andrews.
note: Eliminated Erik Andrews with a Sunset Bomb earlier in the same match.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick
how: Won a 24 Hour/Submission title-for-title, no-disqualification match by knockout, the referee counting Daniel Sinz's arm down three times after outside interference from Randall Crane left him unconscious.
note: Also the reigning VWF Submission Champion at the time, becoming a double champion. Already billed as Thunder Valenkov's title by the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Twelve broadcast (18 December 2003).

lost.source: No document read, or noted in any prior wave's own findings.md, narrates the vacancy.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Thunder Valenkov
how: Pinned Ric Beauty with a Thunder Bomb off the second rope during a tag match pitting the Beauty Brothers against Valenkov and his own partner Kevin Blair, reclaiming the title he had lost off-page before the previous Firestorm.
note: Lost the title again the same night, pinned by his own tag partner Kevin Blair during the Gauntlet battle royal after new majority owner Kingston Cash needled him ringside about his work visa.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: The Lynch Mob

won.source: A recap package on Firestorm (3 May 2004) shows the Lynch Mob taking the titles from the Rodeo Boys; the underlying match, at an untelevised Lynch Mob Lottery card, is not present anywhere in the held record.

note: Both men wrestle a non-title Team Tournament Final loss on the same broadcast, Firestorm (3 May 2004); a VWF Four Corners Tag Team Championship defense against The Unholy Alliance, Hot Property and the Rodeo Boys is announced for the Gauntlet, outside this pass's own reading.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-blackjack

note: Retained against The Legend of Xtreme in a Last Man Standing match on 24 January and against Jack Spade in a 2 out of 3 falls Midtown Madness brawl at Ghost Town Blues, ruled a draw after both men and the referee were knocked out.

label: The Maquilladora
how: pinfall (Permanent Daylight), after Xtreme Tony Cage's return distracted champion Randall Crane out of a submission hold
note: Lost the title when Classy Joey Boy interfered in Maq's next defense and pinned him directly; CAPSMAN and Marcel Klutz, the announced challengers, never reached the ring.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-triple-threat
label: Classy Joey Boy
how: pinfall on champion The Maquilladora, interfering in a title match between Maq and two other men
note: The promotion's own last show before becoming RAW-Vegas; no later document shows this reign challenged or resolved.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Kevin Blair
how: Pinned Thunder Valenkov with a back body drop onto Valenkov's own cane, Lucy, during the Gauntlet battle royal.
note: Attacked Valenkov, Ric Beauty and Rob Beauty with Lucy after his own earlier tag match, then won the title from Valenkov in the closing battle royal the same night. Retained the title by count-out against Flash on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after leaving the ring with the belt rather than answering the referee's count, which eliminated him from the Dog Days tournament; a further challenge from Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) ended with both men walking away from the ring before a decision, the title again not changing hands. Majority owner Kingston Cash declares the championship no longer recognized by the promotion on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) and tries to confiscate the belt; Blair refuses and strikes Cash down, keeping the belt in his own possession with no successor named. Still clutching the same belt, Blair loses to a returning Classy Joey Boy by disqualification in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004) after attacking the referee rather than give it up. Eliminated early from a VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004) after fleeing to the back with the belt; Adam Jennings wins the battle royal and is announced champion by the ring announcer, but Kingston Cash refuses to recognize the change unless Jennings physically takes the belt from Blair. Blair fails to appear for a signed follow-up against Jennings on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), ruled a no contest; Cash instead sends his own new bodyguard G-Gangsta after Jennings, no bell rung. Blair again fails to appear for a defense against Fast Eddie Cutlass on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), another no contest, and runs in with Lucy to chair Jennings after Jennings beats Gangsta later the same show; Cash books Blair against Jennings in an I Quit match for the title at Vegas Violence. Loses the title to Adam Jennings in an I Quit match at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), knocked into the referee before physically knocking Jennings around while refusing to let go of the belt himself; finally says the words after a powerslam over the top rope with both men still gripping the title, then speared, sedated and stretchered out.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Adam "The Hype" Jennings
how: Forced champion Kevin Blair, who never released his own grip on the belt, to say the words in an I Quit match after a powerslam over the top rope left both men still holding the title.
note: Chairs a recovering Sebastian and G-Gangsta backstage the same night. Retains against a masked Billy Bones, billed The Masked Nevadan, on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), forcing the tap with the Hyper Driver before Robbie Caldwell unmasks and tazes the champion in a post-match attack chased off by Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov. Retains again over Robbie Caldwell in a Bring Your Own Weapons match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), finishing him with the Hyper Driver moments after ringside legend Johnny "Hands Of" Stone reclaims his own prosthetic leg, which Caldwell had used as a weapon on the champion. Retains against Paddy O'Shea at March To Madness (2 March 2005) by disqualification after Frank O'Shea's own interference. Retains against the debuting Mad Bomber at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), the Bomber disqualified for refusing to let a bomb-sniffing dog search his pockets. Retains again over the Mad Bomber at End Of March (30 March 2005), pinning him while he is stuck in a bulky training suit. Retained without a challenge at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005): on the line, alongside the Submission and Hardcore Championships, in an eight-man elimination match, but champion Adam Jennings is the final survivor for his own side and is never eliminated.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Thunder Valenkov

won.source: Already billed as reigning VWF 24 Hour Champion by the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Twelve broadcast (18 December 2003) and again on the Kickoff Card (9 January 2004); no document read, or noted in any prior wave's own findings.md, establishes when or how he won the vacant title.

how: Already champion entering the Kickoff Card, retained against Sonicman by disqualification after Lance Voltar interfered and fled with the title belt.
note: After the bell, Capsman's own regular tag partner appeared to unmask himself as an impostor, Evil Capsman, and attacked the fallen Sonicman before the real Capsman ran in to make the save. Retained in a ladder match against The Maquilladora on Firestorm (19 January 2004) after Demonic ran in and struck The Maquilladora with the Pitz of Hell as he neared the top of the ladder. Retained in an I Quit match against Lance Voltar at Ghost Town Blues (19 Feb 2004) with a Thunder Bomb off the top rope into the ring barriers, manager Chris Wheeling interfering mid-match on the champion's behalf.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-24-hour
label: Ric Beauty

won.source: A recap package and Blackbird's own in-ring dialogue on Firestorm (3 May 2004) name Ric Beauty the current VWF 24 Hour Champion; no document in the held record shows him winning the title from Thunder Valenkov.

note: Blindsided by Thunder Valenkov at ringside on Firestorm (3 May 2004); a Triple Threat, expanded by his own brother Rob into a Beauty Brothers tag match against Kevin Blair and Valenkov for the title, is announced for the Gauntlet, outside this pass's own reading.

title: vwf-vegas-2003-tag-team
label: Blaze and Real Deal

won.source: Already billed VWF Tag Team Champions entering Wrestle Style V.2 (27 August 2004); no document in the held record shows how they regained the titles from Hot Property, matching this title's own established pattern of off-page changes.

how: Already champions entering Wrestle Style V.2, retained against the Society of Doom (Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen) by disqualification after O'Malley, not the legal man, locked Real Deal in a Cobra Clutch.
note: No VWF Tag Team Championship match is held on Wrestle Style V.3. None is held on Wrestle Style V.4 or V.5 either. Retains against Capsman and Evil Capsman on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) by disqualification after The Mighty Men run in to break up a Capsman near-fall on Real Deal. Loses the titles to Alcoholics Anonymous (Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen) at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), Real Deal tapping to McQueen's own Devils Snare; lawyer RAR argues the new champions are themselves illegitimate, since the Rodeo Boys were released rather than beaten for the belts, and majority owner Kingston Cash reinstates the Rodeo Boys on the spot to beat down the new champions.

note: Ended when the title was unified into the Vegas Heavyweight Championship, which he won.
